claims.text: A 31-year-old woman was referred to a neurologist in December 2006 for consciousness disorder and fainting. Her main problems were obesity, snoring and waking with a feeling of suffocation; she was depressed, had sleep apnea and myoclonus, and had several episodes of complete loss of consciousness. Examination showed a large Mallampati class III soft palate and EEG focal dysrhythmia with scattered sharp waves. She was on anticonvulsants (lamotrigine for 5 months, later sodium valproate 500 mg per day) and antidepressants.
